Subject: Cap structure — proposed per-invoice vs. annual exposure framing

Hi Thomas / Acme legal team,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Attached is Redwood's current working redline (v3) of the MSA + Order Form. The open item we want to present clearly to your counsel is the limitation of liability framing — we think resolving this quickly will unblock signature.

High-level options we are proposing for discussion (goal = simple, predictable, and aligned with revenue exposure):

1) Aggregate cap = total fees paid under the agreement (contract term) — straightforward but can under-index for long contracts where recent spend is small.
2) Annualized cap = fees paid in prior 12 months (rolling or fixed year) — ties exposure to current run-rate and is common for SaaS.
3) Per-invoice (billing-period) cap = several options: e.g., higher of (a) 3x most recent monthly invoice, or (b) 12 months of fees capped at X — this keeps near-term operational exposure bounded for short bursts but can be complex to administer.

Our commercial team prefers a hybrid that balances predictability for you and protects Redwood against outsized exposure from multi-year accruals. Example illustration: if Acme's first-year committed spend = $1.2M (monthly invoicing at $100k), proposal = greater of (i) 12 months' fees ($1.2M) or (ii) 3x average monthly ($300k) + a baseline remediation carveout for IP/data incidents (separate). Practically that would be \"greater of 12 months' fees or 3x highest monthly invoice in prior 6 months.\"

Carveouts we think are required (standard):
- Gross negligence / willful misconduct (narrowly defined)
- Third-party IP infringement claims tied to Redwood deliverables
- Indemnification obligations (we can keep indemnity caps aligned to the same monetary floor)
- Statutory liabilities (e.g., fraud) — not capped

Open asks for your team:
- Which of the three cap anchors is Acme counsel comfortable with in principle?
- If annualized, do you prefer rolling 12-month or first 12-months post-effective-date?
- If per-invoice hybrid, is the \"3x monthly\" approach administrable for your finance/procurement teams?

I've highlighted the operative sections in the attached redline and added inline comments where we think definition clarifications are required (\"fees paid\", \"billing period\" and reset mechanics). Can we aim to close on a direction this week? I can jump on a 30-minute call with your counsel to walk through examples.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Stephanie — thanks for the clear framing and the worked examples. I've looped in Acme legal (cc) and copied procurement (Sarah) so they can confirm administerability. Initial comments from Acme legal:

- We are generally comfortable with an annualized cap tied to the prior 12 months' paid fees; it matches our internal risk appetite and makes forecasting simple.
- The concern with "greater of" hybrids is auditability — if we need to pick between two mechanisms (12 months vs. 3x monthly), we'll ask for clear calculation rules and a reconciliation period.
- For security/data incidents we need explicit carveouts for direct remediation costs and third-party notification expenses; these should be additive up to a reasonable subset of the cap (we can propose $250k for notification + forensic).

Acme legal also asked if Redwood would accept a hard floor for the cap (e.g., minimum $500k) so we have a lower bound for small pilots.

I'll leave it to our legal team to produce redlines; could you confirm Redwood's tolerance for a minimum floor and whether you can accept a fixed list of reimbursement items that sit outside the cap (notification, regulatory fines? — we assume fines remain uncapped but need clarity).

Thomas
Thomas Reid
Head of Procurement, Acme Inc

Hi Stephanie / team — quick notes from legal counsel (internal):

1) Annualized cap (rolling 12 months) is our preference because it limits risk while remaining tied to operative spend.
2) We cannot accept a cap that excludes statutory liabilities or indemnities — those remain uncapped. Please confirm Redwood's stance.
3) For data/privacy incidents we'd like to carve out direct costs for notification and credit monitoring and also have a limited carveout for third-party claims resulting from Redwood's breach (subject to indemnity procedures).

We prepared a draft redline that: (a) sets the cap at the greater of (i) 12 months' fees or (ii) $500k; (b) enumerates carveouts for notification/forensic (capped at $300k) as additive; (c) clarifies that punitive and statutory penalties are uncapped.

We will upload the mark-up to your shared drive and can meet Monday to go through line-by-line.

— Acme Legal

Stephanie / Karthik — internal note before we jump on the Monday sync: a few commercial considerations to keep in mind

• Pricing impact: if we agree to a $500k floor + 12 months' fees, small pilots may become less attractive unless we discount early months. Suggest we model impact for 3 representative accounts (pilot $20k/month, mid-market $35k/mo, enterprise $120k/mo).

• Ramp language: to avoid punishing early low-spend customers, we can include a 12-month lookback that starts after the "production" milestone or after the first invoice to avoid artificially low caps during POC.

• Implementation: finance needs a one-line calculation algorithm (we propose: cap = max(12-mo paid fees ending on last invoice date, $500k)). If Acme legal insists on notification carveouts additive up to $300k, make sure accounting knows which buckets are non-recurring chargebacks vs. reductions in cap.

I'll join the Monday call and bring the 3-model P&L.

— Marissa
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts

Thomas / Acme legal — thanks for the draft redline and the thoughtful questions. We discussed internally and can accept the compromise below as a path to close:

Final commercial proposal (Redwood):
- Limitation of liability = greater of (i) fees paid in prior 12 months (rolling), or (ii) $500,000 minimum floor.
- Data/privacy: direct notification and remediation costs (up to $300,000) are carved out and additive to the cap; third-party indemnity claims remain subject to the same cap but follow indemnity procedures (notice, defense control, mitigation).
- Statutory penalties and willful fraud remain uncapped.
- Ramp language: the 12-month lookback shall begin on first invoice date; for customers with <12 months of invoices, cap equals actual paid fees to date or the $500k floor, whichever is greater.

If that text aligns with Acme, please confirm and we'll incorporate the redline into the MSA. We believe this balances Acme's forecasting needs and Redwood's exposure profile. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Legal — Commercial Agreements
Redwood Inference
